full_judgment: 13. It further appears that the trial Court on examination of the materials on record held that, only question for determination is whether the plaintiffs could prove that Mohammad Hossain Mia got the settlement through RS Case No. 650/36-37. On analyzing the materials on record it found that the Kabuliyat (Exhibit 4) has been executed on 6.2.1937 and has been accepted on 15-3-1950 and the form on which the said Kabuliat has been prepared appears to have been printed from one "Lucky Press", Chaumuhani, Noakhali on 26-2-1954 and thus the trial Court held that; how a Kabuliat claimed to have been executed on 6-2-1937 and accepted 15-3-1950 can be shown to have been executed in a form printed on 26-2-1954 from Lucky Press, Chaumuhani. It also held that the date of comparing the deed and printing of the Kabuliyat and the date of execution are not the same. Thus the Kabuliyat (Exhibit 4) is not a reliable document and no title and possession can be passed on the basis of such unacceptable document. From the materials on record the trial Court also found that the Government vide Certificate Case No. 201/33-34 auction purchased the suit land on 1-10-1936 which was confirmed on 4-12-1936 and RS Case No. 650/36-37 appears to have been filed and Kabuliyat appears to have been executed on 6-2-1937. So the chronology of dates also show that, after confirmation of auction sale within two months the RS case has been filed which clearly proves that within a year (actually two months) of getting the auction sale confirmed in favour of the Government, Mohammad Hossain Miah created the settlement by the said Kabuliyat.
